target_customer: Consumers in debt who could not afford professional credit counselors
problem: Credit counseling and debt consulting were expensive. Debteye analyzed bank data via Yodlee, prioritized bills and helped fill debt management or settlement forms.
business_model: Consumer subscription planned (free at launch, monthly fee to follow)

founders.name: Paul Zhang
founders.background_notes: Later cofounded Avant and is its CTO per YC page.

founders.name: John Sun
founders.background_notes: All three cofounders were certified credit counselors per TechCrunch.

competitors.name: ReadyForZero
competitors.what: Tracked monthly payments and suggested debt paydown optimizations

competitors.name: Professional debt consulting firms
competitors.what: Incumbent human credit counselors and debt settlement companies

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating accounts through Yodlee and generating forms is routine web work; the domain knowledge of certified counselors was the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Counselor credentials helped credibility, but a rival or Mint style tool could copy the workflow.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company was acquired (acquirer and date not found).

market_need_then: Post 2008 consumer debt stress and expensive counselors; TechCrunch July 2011 framed it as a much cheaper credit counselor.

branding.community_and_virality: A debt relief blog reviewed the product critically ('swing and a miss', getoutofdebt.org).

brand_strength.rationale: Pun on debt and eye with a debt-focused tone; negative association with debt and misspelling risk, little brand press.

outcome_analysis: Debteye launched in July 2011 as a cheaper automated credit counselor built by three certified counselors, one of whom later cofounded Avant. YC lists it as Acquired, but the buyer, date and price were not found in any source. The strength of the exit is unknown, so no failure or success drivers beyond founder domain fit are asserted.
notes: Acquisition details not found in two outcome searches; may be an acquihire. No funding information found. Website not fetched (no site given in queue). Name origin not sourced (the debt and eye pun is not asserted).
